hook.es: Un sistema no tiene por qué existir solo para uno.
hook.en: A system doesn't have to exist for just one.

objective: The repeating pattern noticed in Episode 4 (IntCloudSysOps) gets a name and a shape: Opsly. The architecture forms in layers — Tenant, Blueprint, Modules, Events, Agents, Approvals, Metrics, Learning. This happens before any specific client world exists; Opsly is built as a way of building, not as one product for one client.

metadata.call_to_action: Un blueprint puede convertirse en muchos mundos.

captions.es: De un patrón repetido a un blueprint con nombre.
captions.en: From a repeated pattern to a named blueprint.

metadata.thumbnail_concept: The layered architecture (Tenant/Blueprint/Modules/Events/Agents/Approvals/Metrics/Learning) forming as a glowing vertical structure in the Parallel World, still empty of any tenant-world

notes: Act V of the Origin Saga — see ../../canon/ORIGIN-SAGA.md.

REORDER NOTE: this episode now precedes Peskids (Episode 6), reversed from this season's earlier draft where Blueprint followed Peskids. The Origin Saga places platform-formation before the first tenant — Opsly is built as a general way of building, and Peskids (Ep06) is the first real world to run on it. See ../../canon/CONTINUITY-RULES.md for why this reorder was made and documented rather than left silent.
Theme: naming the pattern — the shift from 'building projects' to 'building a way of building.'
Emotional conflict: ambition growing faster than confidence; the realization that a full platform is a much bigger commitment than another client project.

Visual motif: the layered stack (Tenant -> Blueprint -> Modules -> Events -> Agents -> Approvals -> Metrics -> Learning) rendered as a literal glowing vertical structure, still empty/unpopulated — it gets its first real content in Episode 6.
Cristian realizes his prior 'many lives' (Episode 2) may have been training for exactly this: understanding operation, sales, people, and infrastructure all at once, not just code.
Real event / fictionalization boundary: see ../../canon/TIMELINE.md row 05.
